cues: Innocence to experience: the confident child of the first half becomes someone who has seen what she cannot explain, and it happens exactly at I know not.
Nature as theatre: she never looks at the sun itself, only at what it does.
Death, handled gently: Dickinson wrote dozens of poems about dying, and this is one of the few that is not afraid.
And faith and doubt: the church and the shepherd are all there, but only as what seemed.
A comforting picture, and an honest verb.
